reviews.recommendation_label: Weak Accept — marginally above the acceptance threshold, but would not mind if rejected, dependent on rebuttal
reviews.text_contribution:
The novel framework proposed in this study explicitly models individual variation across three key dimensions—morphology, temporal progression, and developmental stage—to predict embryonic euploidy.
A comprehensive dataset comprising 1,034 embryos was constructed, integrating time-lapse imaging sequences with structured clinical information (7 slices per time point), enabling evaluation grounded in clinical context.
Extensive experimental validation demonstrated superior predictive accuracy compared to existing methods, quantitatively demonstrating the importance of accounting for individual variation.
reviews.text_strengths:
Implements highly innovative modeling approaches (AMRM, ITIM, GDRE)
AMRM: Extracts embryo-specific structural variation features by adaptively combining shared morphological patterns conditioned on clinical information
ITIM: Features an adaptive weighting mechanism that emphasizes critical developmental stages specific to each embryo
GDRE: Utilizes heteroscedastic loss to automatically account for the “uncertainty” of embryos that deviate significantly from standard developmental trajectories, thereby enhancing training stability
Rather than simply combining features, it employs TabGLM to extract relationships between clinical factors and incorporates these insights into the image feature encoding
The team has independently collected clinical data to construct the dataset. Notably, they have gone as far as collecting data specific to different incubator models.
reviews.text_weaknesses:
In the ablation study, removing clinical information resulted in a significant AUC drop from 0.826 to 0.728, indicating that performance may be severely limited in environments with missing clinical data.
While it’s commendable that the paper examines bias differences across incubators in detail, the specific breakdown of each dataset and any actual biases observed remain unclear. Notably, the F1 score shows substantial variation between incubator types, raising questions about the underlying reasons for this discrepancy.
This study divides embryo development into 16 temporal segments for training and evaluation, but different developmental stages likely require varying resolution for accurate euploidy prediction. The authors suggest addressing this through foundation model utilization and temporal attention strategies, but the paper lacks a detailed analysis of which specific time points contribute most significantly to prediction accuracy.
reviews.text_detailed_comments:
I consider this to be a truly remarkable study. While I fully understand that the dataset contains highly sensitive and difficult-to-handle data, given its exceptional value for IVF research, I hope you’ll consider making it publicly available. This would significantly advance the field and I’d appreciate your positive consideration.

This study effectively implements a clear conceptual framework for modeling inter-individual variability across three key dimensions - spatial distribution, temporal dynamics, and uncertainty - to address a critical clinical challenge in IVF embryo evaluation. The research demonstrates particularly high technical innovation. Notably, its design effectively utilizes clinical metadata not merely as supplementary information but as the basis for determining module weights. Furthermore, the construction of the dataset represents highly significant work. The comprehensive evaluation approach, including ablation studies, makes the overall structure exceptionally well-balanced. While some aspects require refinement in the dataset details and result interpretation, these can be addressed through rebuttals. Therefore, I assign a “weak accept” rating.

N/A

title: Boundary-Aware Multi-Granularity Learning for Depression Severity Estimation
abstract: Depression severity estimation is formulated as continuous regression, yet clinical decisions rely on categorical severity grades. This granularity mismatch leads to boundary-agnostic optimization and ordinally unstructured representations. We propose Multi-Granularity Supervision, jointly leveraging continuous scores and ordinal grades as complementary signals. Our key theoretical contribution proves that ordinal supervision induces boundary-aware gradient amplification, where gradient magnitude peaks at clinical thresholds. We instantiate this through Ordinal Consistency Regularization for boundary awareness in prediction space, and Prototype-based Severity Contrastive Learning for ordinal structure in feature space. On AVEC 2013, AVEC 2014, DAIC-WOZ, and E-DAIC, we achieve MAE of 5.06, 5.15, 4.33, and 5.02 respectively, establishing new state-of-the-art across all benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/aqlzh/BAMGL_Depression.
